name: National Supercomputing Center in Taiyuan
developer: Shanxi Province / Shanxi Transformation Comprehensive Reform Demonstration Zone
notes: China Daily (Shanxi) lists the National Supercomputing Center in Taiyuan among Shanxi's national-level innovation platforms (15 national platforms province-wide), alongside the Third-Generation Semiconductor National Technology Innovation Center. Taiyuan's flagship supercomputing facility supports AI, quantum information and integrated-circuit research. MW not disclosed.

name: Baidu Cloud Computing (Yangquan) Center - Phase 1
notes: Baidu's Cloud Computing Center settled in Yangquan in 2012; phase 1 had RMB 4.7 billion investment, 12 hectares construction area and hosts more than 160,000 servers - Baidu's first large-scale data center, reported to lead Asia in data storage scale, computing power and energy efficiency. Located in Yangquan Economic and Technological Development Zone. MW not disclosed.

name: Baidu Cloud Computing (Yangquan) Center - Phase 2
notes: Phase 2 signed and groundbreaking held Nov 21, 2019 in Yangquan Economic and Technological Development Zone with RMB 1.4 billion investment, 8.6 hectares construction area, planned to add 40,000 servers supporting search, intelligent cloud, AI and intelligent driving services. MW not disclosed.

name: LvLiang Cloud Computing Center
developer: Lvliang city (with NUDT/National University of Defense Technology)
notes: TOP500 lists LvLiang Cloud Computing Center as site of the Tianhe-2 LvLiang system (NUDT, Intel Xeon E5-2692v2 + Xeon Phi, 174,720 cores, 2.07 PFlop/s Rmax), ranked in the TOP500 list continuously from Nov 2014; China Daily reported Lvliang fostering a big data industry around the center. Cloud/supercomputing facility operational since 2014. MW not disclosed.

name: Linfen Digital Economy Park
notes: Report on Linfen's digital economy park notes the park focuses on information-technology innovation and application industries represented by big data, cloud computing and electronic information; part of Linfen's digital-economy push. No specific data center or MW disclosed; evidence weak/aggregate.

name: Chengdu Intelligent Computing Center
developer: Chengdu Pidu District government with Huawei (Ascend ecosystem)
notes: Officially launched May 10, 2022 in Pidu District as the largest AI computing center in Southwest China and a sample project of the 'East Data West Computing' national integrated computing network's Chengdu-Chongqing hub node; includes a 300P AI computing platform and urban intelligent-brain platform, built on Huawei Cloud Stack and Ascend AI infrastructure. MW not disclosed.

name: Chengdu Supercomputing Center (National Supercomputing Center in Chengdu)
developer: Chengdu municipal government / Sichuan Tianfu New Area
notes: First national supercomputing center completed and put into operation in western China; started trial operation September 2020 in Tianfu New Area (Chengdu Science City) with max computing speed of about 100 million billion calculations per second (~100 PFLOPS); cooperated with 200+ institutions. MW not disclosed.

name: Tianfu Cloud Computing Center
developer: China Telecom Sichuan with Sichuan Tianfu New Area Administrative Committee
notes: Construction launch announced May 13, 2026 via cooperation agreement between Sichuan Tianfu New Area and China Telecom Sichuan; RMB 2 billion total investment, ~28,000 sqm building area south of Xinglong Lake, will provide 3,600P intelligent computing power for AI training and large-model development; completion expected 2027; positioned as China Telecom's '4+4+31+X' core western-region computing node and key expansion of the Chengdu Tianfu data center cluster. MW not disclosed.

name: Tianfu Data Center Cluster (Chengdu-Chongqing hub)
notes: NDRC official reply (Feb 2022) approving the Chengdu-Chongqing region as a national hub node of the integrated computing power network ('East Data West Computing'), establishing the Tianfu Data Center Cluster with starting zones in Chengdu's Shuangliu District, Pidu District and Jianyang City, plus the Chongqing cluster; cluster-level designation under which individual Chengdu projects (e.g. Chengdu Intelligent Computing Center, Tianfu Cloud Computing Center) are built. Capacity/MW not applicable at cluster level.

name: China Western Information Center
notes: Data Center Map lists China Western Information Center in the new Tianfu area of Chengdu High-tech Zone; site covers 60,030 sqm, building area about 220,000 sqm with 30,000 sqm of IDC space - China Telecom's flagship western-region facility in Chengdu. MW not disclosed; aggregate directory source.

name: Aba Prefecture Intelligent Computing Industrial Park and Low-altitude Economy Intelligent Computing Center
developer: Aba Prefecture government (with State Grid Sichuan Aba Power Supply Co.)
notes: Sichuan Daily: groundbreaking ceremony held March 31, 2025 in Hongyuan County for the Aba Prefecture intelligent computing industrial park and low-altitude economy intelligent computing center; positioned as a 'green power + computing' integration demonstration using abundant hydropower/solar and natural high-altitude cooling; plans to expand to Aba County and Zoige County; integrated into the 'East Data West Computing' national push. MW not disclosed.
